__readme: Shared parity fixtures for the versioned eval VERDICT POLICY contract (verdictPolicyVersion 2). Loaded by sdk/tests/contract-verdict-policy.test.ts in mcpjam-inspector (zod: evalVerdictDecisionSchema / evalCaseVerdictAggregationSchema / evalRateMeasurementSchema / resolvedEvalValidityPolicySchema in sdk/src/contract/verdict-policy.ts) and by sdk/tests/eval-verdict-policy-schema-json.test.ts (the GENERATED JSON Schema, through ajv). It is written to be copied VERBATIM into mcpjam-backend as the B4-W2 mirror corpus, exactly as score-contract-parity-fixtures.json already is: the backend cannot import @mcpjam/sdk into convex/ default-runtime code, so a shared fixture file is the only common ground truth. Copy it byte for byte; do not re-author it. LOAD RULE: strip EVERY key whose name starts with '__' before handing a row to a validator; they are fixture annotations (__kind, __label, __why, __structural) and every object in this contract is closed, so a payload still carrying them would be rejected for the wrong reason — turning an accept row into a false failure and, worse, a reject row into a false success. DISPATCH: '__kind' selects the validator — 'decision', 'case', 'rate' or 'policy'. '__structural' says whether the GENERATED JSON Schema must reject the row too (true) or whether it is a cross-field rule only zod can express (false); the json-schema test asserts BOTH directions, so a mislabelled row fails loudly instead of being excused. NOT EXPRESSIBLE IN JSON: NaN, Infinity and -Infinity are not JSON values, so the non-finite rejections live in the zod test itself rather than here. AGGREGATION COHORT: each row is an INPUT (a case's configured trial count, its effective pass threshold, and one entry per trial carrying a lifecycle status, an optional task verdict and an optional evaluator-error flag) plus the EXPECTED per-case aggregation output. This wave ships no aggregator: the rows pin the arithmetic a future producer must reproduce, and the test derives the counts from the trial list to prove the expected output is self-consistent. DERIVATION RULES, which the mirror must match: a trial is ATTEMPTED unless its status is pending, skipped or cancelled — a RUNNING trial has begun and stays in the attempted denominator, while a CANCELLED one is withdrawn from every denominator so that stopping a run cannot report it as incomplete; it is ELIGIBLE when it completed with a task verdict and no evaluator error; passRate is passed over eligible; completionRate is completed over attempted; observedStability is max(passed, failed) over eligible; mixedVerdict is true exactly when both a pass and a fail were graded; a zero denominator is notMeasured with a null value; and validity is decided BEFORE the task verdict, so a run whose validity fails is inconclusive with validity-only reasons. When the contract shape changes, edit the zod source, regenerate the JSON Schema artifacts, AND update this fixture in the same PR. IDENTITY: a case aggregate is keyed by caseId PLUS its optional executionVariant (the provider/model pair a hosted fan-out ran it under), configuredTrials is the PER-VARIANT repetitions count, and one case may not mix variant-keyed and unkeyed aggregates. REASONS: a decision's reasons array must be EXACTLY the checks its own measurements failed — in the vocabulary's order, nothing missing and nothing invented — and once validity holds it is exactly the one reason its cases produced.

accept.__label: repetitions 1 — the low boundary of the portable range, single passing trial
accept.__why: repetitions is the suite file's own 1..100 range. One trial is a legal suite, and a 1/1 pass rate against an inherited 0.5 threshold passes.

accept.__label: repetitions 100 — the high boundary, 0.6 pass rate over the maximum trial count
accept.__why: 100 is MAX_REPETITIONS in the portable suite-file contract. The hosted platform's much lower per-case cap is a product limit and is deliberately NOT the schema cap.

accept.__label: suite inheritance and case override — 0.5 inherited, 1.0 overridden, both pass
accept.__why: effectivePassThreshold is the RESOLVED value: c_inherited carries the suite default and c_override carries its own. Equality passes on both (0.5 >= 0.5, 1.0 >= 1.0).

accept.__label: mixed pass and fail at threshold 0.5 exactly — equality passes
accept.__why: mixedVerdict is true because both a pass and a fail were graded. observedStability is max(1,1)/2 = 0.5: a case that disagreed with itself as much as it possibly could.

accept.__label: all pass at threshold 1.0 — stability 1, no mixed verdict
accept.__why: Threshold 1 is the strictest measurable bar and 4/4 meets it exactly. Stability 1 here means agreement; the all-fail row below shows why stability alone is not quality.

accept.__label: all fail at threshold 0 — stability 1, pass rate 0, and the case PASSES
accept.__why: The two halves of the trap in one row: observedStability is max(0,3)/3 = 1 for a case that never passed, and a threshold of 0 is a real, satisfiable bar (0 >= 0) as long as something was graded. Contrast the zero-eligible row, which is inconclusive at the same threshold.

accept.__label: all fail at threshold 0.5 — failed, not inconclusive
accept.__why: Three trials that ran to `completed` with a failing task verdict. Lifecycle and task verdict are orthogonal: this is the NORMAL way a case fails, and nothing here maps a status onto a verdict.

accept.__label: one unmeasured case forces the whole run inconclusive — even at threshold 0
accept.__why: c_unmeasured graded nothing, so its own verdict is inconclusive and validity does not hold for the run. Its threshold of 0 is irrelevant: 'nothing was graded' is not 'everything graded passed'. The completion floor is relaxed and both ungraded trials were ATTEMPTED, so the ONLY thing failing validity is the unmeasured case.

accept.__label: explicit minEligibleTrials 4 met with a timed-out trial — completion exactly 0.8
accept.__why: Two boundaries at once. The explicit floor REPLACES the default coverage rule, so a trial that was attempted and never graded is no longer disqualifying by itself; and completion is 4/5 = 0.8, which meets the 0.8 default because the comparison is >=.

accept.__label: evaluator error rate exactly 0.1 — the ceiling is inclusive
accept.__why: 1/10 evaluator errors sits exactly on maxEvaluatorErrorRate. The evaluator-error trial still COMPLETED, so it counts as completed for the completion rate while being excluded from eligibility: the two denominators are different populations, which is why exclusions travel per rate.

accept.__label: pass rate 0.5 at threshold 0.5 with two trials each way
accept.__why: observedStability is max(2,2)/4 = 0.5, the minimum a two-outcome case can have.

accept.__label: threshold 1.0 with one failure — failed
accept.__why: 2/3 is below 1.0, so the case fails and the suite fails with it. Validity held: this is a measured, trustworthy failure.

accept.__label: pending and skipped trials leave the attempted denominator — a running one does not
accept.__why: A skipped trial was never asked for and a pending one never started, so both leave BOTH denominators: attempted is 5, not 7. A RUNNING trial has begun, so it stays in the attempted denominator and drags completion to 4/5 — the difference between 'not started' and 'not finished', which is the whole reason notTerminal is one exclusion reason and not two.

accept.__label: executionFailed and timedOut exclusions — attempted but never gradeable
accept.__why: Both trials were attempted, so they stay in the completion denominator (3/5 = 0.6) and drag it down; neither has a task verdict, so both leave the eligibility denominator. That asymmetry is the whole reason a rate carries its own exclusions.

accept.__label: rate — zero denominator is notMeasured with a null value
accept.__why: The one shape this envelope exists to make unrepresentable: 0/0 rendering as 0 (a failing rate) or as 1 (a passing one). notMeasured pins value to null, which no threshold comparison can accept.

accept.__label: rate — a repeating quotient is carried at full double precision
accept.__why: value is exactly numerator/denominator in IEEE-754, not a rounded display number. A producer that rounds ships a rate that disagrees with its own counts.

accept.__label: rate — a measured ZERO is not the same thing as notMeasured
accept.__why: 0/4 is a real measurement whose value is 0. Collapsing it into notMeasured (or the reverse) is how a suite that failed everything gets reported as untested, and vice versa.

accept.__label: policy — omitted minEligibleTrials resolves to the default coverage rule
accept.__why: The resolved form of the suite-file default. Omission is a STRICTER rule than a numeric floor, not a weaker one: every configured trial attempted AND at least one gradeable trial, with minGradeableTrials carried in the value rather than in prose.

accept.__label: policy — an explicit minEligibleTrials replaces the coverage rule
accept.__why: Explicit N tolerates unattempted trials by design: the author has said how much evidence is enough.

accept.__label: policy — thresholds at the extremes of the unit interval
accept.__why: 0 and 1 are legal fractions on both knobs. Percent-shaped values are rejected structurally; see the reject cohort.

accept.__label: default coverage rule — one configured trial never attempted, so inconclusive
accept.__why: 3/3 of what ran passed, and the run still says nothing: the default coverage rule (omitted minEligibleTrials) requires every configured trial to have been attempted. This is the row the old 'absent means no minimum' comment would have reported as a confident pass.

accept.__label: no gradeable trials at all — inconclusive, never failed
accept.__why: Setup never succeeded, so nothing was graded. Reporting this as failed would blame the server for our own environment.

accept.__label: completion rate 0.6 below the 0.8 floor — inconclusive even though coverage was met
accept.__why: The three checks are INDEPENDENT: the explicit eligibility floor is satisfied (3 >= 3) and the run is still inconclusive because two fifths of the ATTEMPTED trials never completed.

accept.__label: evaluator error rate 0.2 above the 0.1 ceiling — inconclusive
accept.__why: 8/8 of the gradeable trials passed. The grader failed on a fifth of the run, so the run does not describe the server: a broken judge is not a broken server.

accept.__label: nothing attempted — both validity rates are notMeasured and no floor is satisfiable
accept.__why: A notMeasured completion rate cannot meet a 0.8 floor and a notMeasured evaluator-error rate cannot satisfy a 0.1 ceiling. Absence of measurement never passes a bound, in either direction.

accept.__label: a cancelled trial leaves BOTH denominators — cancelling cannot make a run look incomplete
accept.__why: The completion floor is 0.9 here on purpose: under the rejected reading (cancelled stays attempted) completion would be 4/5 = 0.8 and the run would be INCONCLUSIVE — a verdict about the server manufactured by a human pressing stop. Withdrawing the trial from every denominator leaves 4/4 = 1 over the trials that were allowed to finish, and the four graded trials still decide the run.

accept.__label: one case fanned across two provider/model variants — the weaker variant fails the run
accept.__why: A hosted run fans ONE case across provider/model pairs and numbers each pair's iterations from 1, so identity is caseId PLUS executionVariant. Both rows carry the same caseId and the same configuredTrials of 2 (the portable per-variant repetitions), and the run FAILS because every measured aggregate must meet its threshold — merging the pairs into one row would both hide which model regressed and inflate configuredTrials past the portable range.

accept.__label: an execution variant may name a model with no provider
accept.__why: provider is the same optional disambiguating hint the suite file's defaults treat it as, so a run that fans across models within one provider identifies its variants by model alone. Omitting the whole executionVariant means something different again — 'this run did not fan out' — and never matches a variant-keyed row.

reject.__label: decision — no verdictPolicyVersion at all (legacy row, not a v2 one)
reject.__why: The load-bearing rejection of this wave. A row produced before v2 carries no version, and defaulting it to 2 would restate percent-threshold numbers under trial-fraction semantics. Absence is v1; it is never filled in.

reject.__label: decision — verdictPolicyVersion 1
reject.__why: A version this contract does not describe is refused rather than best-effort parsed.

reject.__label: decision — verdictPolicyVersion as a string
reject.__why: The version is a numeric literal. A string that looks like it is still not it.

reject.__label: decision — an unknown top-level field
reject.__why: Every object in this contract is closed, matching the Convex v.object mirror. A legacy percent field arriving alongside v2 fields must fail loudly, not be ignored by one validator and rejected by the other.

reject.__label: decision — an empty reasons array
reject.__why: A verdict with no recorded reason is unauditable. There is always at least one.

reject.__label: decision — no cases
reject.__why: A decision over nothing is not a decision.

reject.__label: decision — a reason outside the closed vocabulary
reject.__why: Reasons are a closed enum so consumers can branch on them exhaustively.

reject.__label: decision — 'incomplete' is the LEGACY verdict word, not this vocabulary
reject.__why: The shipped per-case chain summary says incomplete; this contract says inconclusive. Accepting both would leave two spellings of one state in the same system.

reject.__label: decision — a percent-shaped pass threshold (50)
reject.__why: The single most likely migration bug from the legacy percent thresholds: 50 meaning 50%. It is out of [0,1] and rejected structurally, in the JSON Schema as well as in zod.

reject.__label: decision — a negative pass threshold
reject.__why: Below the unit interval.

reject.__label: decision — a percent-shaped completion floor (80)
reject.__why: Same trap on the validity policy.

reject.__label: decision — configuredTrials above the portable maximum of 100
reject.__why: MAX_REPETITIONS is imported from the suite-file contract rather than restated, so the two cannot drift apart.

reject.__label: decision — configuredTrials of 0
reject.__why: A case configured to run nothing is not a case.

reject.__label: decision — a fractional trial count
reject.__why: Counts are integers.

reject.__label: decision — a caseId with whitespace
reject.__why: Ids travel through file paths, CLI arguments and URLs; the charset is the URL-safe one.

reject.__label: rate — 'measured' with a zero denominator
reject.__why: 0/0 dressed up as a measured 0. This is the exact shape the discriminated union exists to make impossible: a rate that never measured anything but compares as a failing score.

reject.__label: rate — 'notMeasured' with a value of 0 instead of null
reject.__why: The other direction of the same bug: a null-valued state carrying a comparable number.

reject.__label: rate — 'notMeasured' with a non-zero denominator
reject.__why: Trials in the denominator mean it WAS measured. The branch pins denominator to 0 so the two cannot be claimed at once.

reject.__label: rate — a value above 1
reject.__why: Out of the unit interval, whatever the counts say.

reject.__label: rate — an exclusion reason outside the closed vocabulary
reject.__why: The exclusions object is closed on purpose: an open map would silently count a typo'd reason under a key nobody reads.

reject.__label: rate — a third measurement state
reject.__why: There are two states. 'Partially measured' is a rate over a smaller denominator, and the exclusions already say so.

reject.__label: rate — a rounded value that is not its own quotient
reject.__why: 0.33 is not 1/3. A rounded rate stops matching the counts it ships beside, which is precisely how a hosted rate and a re-derived one come to disagree.

reject.__label: rate — numerator greater than denominator
reject.__why: Both numbers are in range and the pair is impossible. Only a cross-field rule catches it.

reject.__label: decision — mixedVerdict false with both a pass and a fail graded
reject.__why: mixedVerdict is derived, not asserted: it is true exactly when both outcomes appeared.

reject.__label: decision — observedStability that is not max(passed, failed) over eligible
reject.__why: A stability of 1 on a case that split 1-1. Stability is a derived number and this is the misreport the formula is pinned against.

reject.__label: decision — passed + failed does not equal eligible
reject.__why: An eligible trial is one with a task verdict, so there is no third bucket for it to hide in.

reject.__label: decision — eligible trials exceeding attempted trials
reject.__why: A trial cannot be graded without having been attempted.

reject.__label: decision — a case with zero eligible trials claiming it passed at threshold 0
reject.__why: The vacuous pass. Nothing was graded, so there is no evidence to pass on, and a threshold of 0 does not manufacture any.

reject.__label: decision — validity does not hold, yet the run reports failed
reject.__why: Completion is 0.5, under the 0.8 floor, so the run did not measure the server. Calling that a failure blames the server for the harness; the phase order exists to stop exactly this.

reject.__label: decision — holds:true asserted over measurements that fail the policy
reject.__why: holds is checked against the rates it summarizes. A producer cannot assert validity it did not have.

reject.__label: decision — an inconclusive run citing a task reason
reject.__why: Validity is evaluated first and did not hold, so no task-verdict conclusion was reached. Recording one claims a phase that never ran.

reject.__label: decision — a passed run missing allMeasuredCasesMetThreshold
reject.__why: The suite-level pass has exactly one reason, and a per-case reason is not it.

reject.__label: decision — suite totals that are not the sum over cases
reject.__why: The suite-level counts are the sum of the per-case counts. A drifting total is how a validity rate ends up measured over a population that does not exist.

reject.__label: decision — a completion rate measured over the wrong denominator
reject.__why: Each rate's denominator names the population it measured. A completion rate over 1 attempted trial when 2 were attempted is a stale numerator with a plausible-looking value.

reject.__label: decision — the same reason recorded twice
reject.__why: Reasons are an audit trail, and a duplicated entry makes a consumer counting them wrong.

reject.__label: case — inconclusive claimed on a case that graded two trials
reject.__why: Eligible trials exist, so the case WAS measured and owes a passed/failed verdict.

reject.__label: case — failed claimed on a pass rate that met the threshold
reject.__why: 0.5 >= 0.5. Equality passes, at every threshold including 0 and 1, and this row is the one that would quietly flip a boundary case.

reject.__label: case — a SUITE-level reason on a case
reject.__why: The reason vocabulary is shared but not interchangeable: a case records why IT concluded, and 'all measured cases' is not a fact a single case knows.

reject.__label: decision — a nested CASE rate whose value is not its own quotient
reject.__why: The aggregate schemas embed the structural rate schema, so the quotient refinement only runs if the aggregate validator invokes it. A 0.75 shipped beside 1/1 is the drift that makes a hosted rate and a re-derived one disagree, one level down where nobody looks.

reject.__label: decision — a nested VALIDITY rate whose value is not its own quotient
reject.__why: Same refinement, the other nesting site: validity's own completion rate must be the quotient of the counts it ships with, or the check that decides whether a run says anything is comparing an invented number against the floor.

reject.__label: decision — a nested VALIDITY rate with more errors than attempts
reject.__why: More evaluator errors than attempted trials is arithmetically impossible, and every field here is independently legal — the value is a fraction in [0,1] and the counts are non-negative integers — so only the nested refinement can catch the pair.

reject.__label: decision — an inconclusive run omitting checks that actually failed
reject.__why: reasons is an audit trail: this run also failed its coverage floor, its evaluator-error measurement and its only case, and a list naming one of the four cannot be reconciled with the measurements it ships beside.

reject.__label: decision — an inconclusive run citing a validity check that PASSED
reject.__why: The eligibility floor was met (3 >= 3). Accusing it anyway makes the reason list unusable for diagnosis, which is the only thing it is for.

reject.__label: decision — the right reasons in the wrong order
reject.__why: Order is part of the contract, not presentation: a hosted decision and an SDK decision are compared BYTE for byte, so the same run must not be able to serialize its reasons two ways.

reject.__label: decision — a passed run adding a per-CASE reason to the suite reason
reject.__why: casePassRateMetThreshold is a case's reason for its own verdict. A suite decision records the suite-level reason and nothing else, or consumers cannot tell how many cases the list is talking about.

reject.__label: decision — two aggregates for the same case AND the same execution variant
reject.__why: Identity is caseId plus executionVariant. Two rows sharing it are two answers to one question, and every consumer that groups by that key would keep whichever it saw last.

reject.__label: decision — one case with a variant-keyed aggregate AND an unkeyed one
reject.__why: An omitted executionVariant means 'this run did not fan out', not 'any variant'. A case cannot be both fanned out and not.

reject.__label: decision — an execution variant carrying an unknown field
reject.__why: The variant is a closed identity, not a bag of execution settings: a temperature here would make two rows with the same provider/model 'different' and silently un-merge a comparison.

reject.__label: decision — an execution variant with an empty model
reject.__why: An empty model is not an identity. It would collide with every other unnamed variant while claiming to be a fan-out row.

roundTrip.__label: roundTrip — a fully measured decision with empty exclusion tallies
roundTrip.__why: Every exclusion object here is `{}`: a reason that excluded nothing is OMITTED rather than written as 0. Parsing must not materialize those zeros, or the payload stops being byte-stable through canonicalJson.

roundTrip.__label: roundTrip — mixed exclusions, explicit coverage floor
roundTrip.__why: The exclusion tallies differ between the eligibility rates and the completion rate on the same case: the cancelled and skipped trials leave both, so the two tallies agree here while the DENOMINATORS do not (3 eligible over 3 attempted out of 5 configured). A round trip must preserve both tallies and must not merge them into one.

roundTrip.__label: roundTrip — a notMeasured rate keeps its null value and its zero counts
roundTrip.__why: null must survive as null. A parser that coerced it to 0 would turn 'not measured' into a failing measurement.

aggregation.__label: mixed pass and fail — 2 of 4 passed at threshold 0.5
aggregation.__why: passRate 2/4 = 0.5 meets the threshold exactly; mixedVerdict true; observedStability max(2,2)/4 = 0.5.
3/3 = 1 meets the strictest measurable bar. Stability 1 and mixedVerdict false.

aggregation.__label: all fail — stability 1 and pass rate 0
aggregation.__why: The canonical misread: perfect stability on a case that never passed once. Stability describes agreement, not quality.

aggregation.__label: zero eligible — threshold 0 does not rescue it
aggregation.__why: Both rates over eligibility are notMeasured, so the verdict is inconclusive and the reason is caseHasNoEligibleTrials. A threshold of 0 is a bar for MEASURED cases. The cancelled trial is withdrawn from EVERY denominator, so the 0/1 completion is the setup_failed trial alone: it was attempted and never completed.

aggregation.__label: cancelled and skipped exclusions on one case
aggregation.__why: Skipped leaves both denominators (never run) and so does cancelled (execution began, then WITHDRAWN from every denominator): completion is 3/3 = 1 over the trials that were allowed to finish, while passRate is 2/3. Cancelling a run must not be able to report the server as incomplete.

aggregation.__label: setup_failed and evaluator-error exclusions on one case
aggregation.__why: setupFailed was attempted and never completed; the evaluator error DID complete but produced no gradeable verdict. Completion 3/4 = 0.75, eligibility 2/4.

aggregation.__label: executionFailed and timedOut exclusions on one case
aggregation.__why: Both non-gradeable trials were attempted, so they stay in the completion denominator (3/5 = 0.6) while leaving eligibility. A lifecycle failure is not a task failure: neither trial has a task verdict to grade.

aggregation.__label: non-terminal trials — a roll-up taken mid-run
aggregation.__why: notTerminal splits: a PENDING trial never started, so it leaves both denominators, while a RUNNING one has begun and stays in attempted — a mid-run roll-up that called it never-attempted would report full completion of a run that is still going. Completion is 2/3, not 2/2.

aggregation.__label: threshold 0 with a measured failure — passes
aggregation.__why: 0 >= 0. A threshold of 0 says 'I only need the case to have run', and it was measured, so it passes.
The repetitions-1 boundary: one trial, an all-or-nothing rate of 1.

aggregation.__label: 100 trials, threshold 0.5, one failure short of nothing
aggregation.__why: The repetitions-100 boundary. 0.51 clears 0.5; stability is 0.51, barely better than a coin.
